ruling.recommended_action: Reverse the $6.61 rider-side cancellation fee and issue a voucher for $6.61 under NS-7; no account action against the driver.

Accepted in substance but misdirected: it is true the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and no arrival was recorded [F3][F4], which is exactly why NS-1 earns him nothing; a null timeline cannot be used to keep a fee that NS-4 says is not chargeable [F2].

Absence of chat or misconduct is irrelevant to entitlement: NS-4 makes a cancellation inside 3 minutes non-chargeable without any rider fault [F2][F7], and the driver's statement 'I was on my way' [F8] is a statement that yields to the timeline records [F2][F3][F4].

Conceded and neutral: normal traffic, no incidents and fair weather [F9][F10][F11] mean the driver was simply driving [F1], which rebuts any fabricated-arrival allegation but supplies no NS-1 or NS-3 basis for charging the rider.

The amount is arithmetically $6.61 with no surge [F5][F6], but arithmetic correctness is not entitlement; NS-4 charges nothing inside the 3-minute window [F2], and NS-7 supplies the voucher/30-day route, not a basis to keep the fee.

Accepted as to profile: F13 cannot decide the case and no flag applies since there was no 'I'm Here' tap and no trip completed without a rider [F4]; this disposes of the rider's C6 add-on, not of the refund itself [F2][F5].

The profile facts (3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show) [F13] cannot ground an account action here: NS-2's flag limb requires an 'I'm Here' tap while off-location and there was no tap at all [F4], and RD-6 does not apply because this is not a route-deviation case with an RD-2 refund.
